items.zu: zu is for people and some places. A city takes nach: nach Berlin.
items.in: in is used for countries with an article. A city takes nach.

items.nach: nach is for cities and countries without an article. die Schweiz has one.
items.in der: in der is Dativ (position). We are travelling there, so Akkusativ: in die.

items.aus das: aus always takes the Dativ: aus dem.
items.im: im means in dem, „inside“. Coming from a place is aus.

items.aus: aus is for places and materials. A person as the source is von.

items.zu: zu means „to someone“. Being at someone's place is bei.

items.in den: in den is Akkusativ (movement). Sitting is a position: Dativ.

items.auf die: auf die is Akkusativ (movement). The horses are standing: Dativ.
items.an der: an der would mean „at the edge of“. On the meadow is auf der.

items.auf der: auf der is Dativ (position). Bringing is movement: Akkusativ.
items.in der: in der is Dativ (position). Bringing is movement: Akkusativ.

items.zu: zu Hause means „at home“. Going home is nach Hause.

items.nach: nach Hause means „going home“. Staying at home is zu Hause.

items.Um: Um is for clock times. Days take am.
Um is for clock times. Months take im.

items.seit: seit is for something that is still going on.
items.in: in einer Woche means one week from now.

items.auf dem: auf dem is Dativ. Blick auf takes the Akkusativ.
items.in den: in den does not fit with Blick.
